3. Data Sources

Observed Data

Data were provided by Dr. Kenneth Kunkel of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA’s) Cooperative Institute for Climate and Satellites (CICS), who analyzed minimum daily temperature records from weather stations throughout the contiguous 48 states. Temperature measurements come from weather stations in NOAA’s Cooperative Observer Program (COOP). This is the same source featured in EPA’s Length of Growing Season indicator.

Model Outputs

This pairing uses daily downscaled outputs from the Seasonal Trends and Analysis of Residuals Empirical-Statistical Downscaling Model (STAR-ESDM) (Hayhoe et al., 2024). STAR-ESDM is one of two downscaling approaches incorporated in the Fifth National Climate Assessment, with the other being Locally Constructed Analogs version 2 (LOCA2). Both are statistically downscaled ensemble products, downscaled to the NOAA nClimGrid product, that provide a nominally 5-kilometer grid over the CONUS.

This pairing presents downscaled STAR-ESDM outputs from 16 global climate models (GCMs) within the World Climate Research Programme (WCRP) Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) suite. Specific runs are noted in parentheses:

  • ACCESS-CM2 (r1i1p1f1)
  • ACCESS-ESM1-5 (r1i1p1f1)
  • BCC-CSM2-MR (r1i1p1f1)
  • CanESM5 (r1i1p1f1)
  • EC-Earth3 (r1i1p1f1)
  • FGOALS-g3 (r1i1p1f1)
  • GFDL-ESM4 (r1i1p1f1)
  • INM-CM4-8 (r1i1p1f1)
  • INM-CM5-0 (r1i1p1f1)
  • IPSL-CM6A-LR (r1i1p1f1)
  • MIROC6 (r1i1p1f1)
  • MPI-ESM1-2-HR (r1i1p1f1)
  • MPI-ESM1-2-LR (r1i1p1f1)
  • MRI-ESM2-0 (r1i1p1f1)
  • NorESM2-LM (r1i1p1f1)
  • NorESM2-MM (r1i1p1f1)

Specifically, this analysis uses the “tasmin” variable, which represents minimum surface air temperature.

4. Data Availability

Observed Data

The project team obtained the data for this indicator from Dr. Kenneth Kunkel at NOAA CICS. Dr. Kunkel had published an earlier version of this analysis in the peer-reviewed literature (Kunkel et al., 2004), and he provided the team with an updated file containing growing season data through 2023, aggregated by state and nationwide.

All raw COOP data are maintained by NOAA’s National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI) (formerly the National Climatic Data Center). Complete COOP data, embedded definitions, and data descriptions can be downloaded from the NCEI COOP site. There are no confidentiality issues that could limit accessibility, but some portions of the data set might need to be formally requested. Complete metadata for the COOP data set can be found at NCEI’s “Station Histories” site and at the National Weather Service’s (NWS’s) COOP site.

Model Outputs

STAR-ESDM downscaled outputs were obtained from the publicly available PCMDI: Earth System Model Evaluation Project. The underlying CMIP6 climate model outputs are also publicly available. The overall technical documentation for this effort identifies the organizational ownership and direct source links for each of the individual models.
